key_insight: Building a very large, diverse video reasoning suite enables systematic study and scaling of spatiotemporal reasoning (continuity, interaction, causality) that text alone cannot capture.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of large-scale training and evaluation data needed to study and benchmark video-level reasoning and its scaling behavior across models.
method: Assemble a large, diverse corpus of videos annotated for spatiotemporal reasoning phenomena (continuity, interaction, causality, temporal localization).
Define a suite of standardized tasks and unified evaluation metrics that probe multi-step and temporal reasoning capabilities.
Conduct scaling studies (varying dataset size and model capacity) to quantify how video reasoning improves with more data and compute and to surface failure modes.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a standardized benchmark and empirical scaling insights to accelerate development of models that truly understand temporal dynamics and causal interactions in video.
visual_elements: Dataset pipeline diagram: collection → annotation → train/val/test splits
Annotated example sequences showing task types (e.g., causal chain, object interaction, temporal continuity)
Scaling curves: model performance vs dataset size / compute showing trends and plateaus
Task taxonomy infographic mapping reasoning categories (continuity, interaction, causality) to concrete evaluation tasks
paper_title: A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite
paper_authors: Maijunxian Wang, Ruisi Wang, Juyi Lin, Ran Ji, Thaddäus Wiedemer
